latest.title: Made Tech secures largest contract in its history
latest.content:
18 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 0300R
Made Tech Group PLC
18 August 2026
MADE TECH GROUP PLC
("Made Tech" or the "Group")
Made Tech secures largest contract in its history
Upgrading Revenue and EBITDA guidance for the second time in 2026
London, 18 August 2026
-
Made Tech Group Plc
, (AIM:MTEC) a leading provider of digital, data and technology services to the UK public sector, is pleased to announce that it has been appointed as part of a consortium to a significant new four-year contract with a UK government department. The total contract value attributable to Made Tech is expected to be approximately £40 million over the life of the four-year contract award (the "
Award
"), making it the largest contract award in the Company's history.
Revenue from the Award is expected to commence in FY27, with a more significant contribution expected in FY28. As a result, the Board now expects revenue for FY27 to be in the range of £63 million to £66 million and adjusted EBITDA for FY27 to be in the range of £6.3 million to £6.6 million, ahead of current market expectations.* The Group will be reporting its FY26 final results in September and will provide further colour on the outlook at this stage.
As announced in its recent trading update, sales bookings accelerated significantly in H226. Together with the Award, this has increased the current Contracted Backlog to approximately £115 million, providing increased revenue visibility into FY27 and beyond
.
Rory MacDonald, CEO of Made Tech, commented:
"This is the largest contract award in our history and marks an important milestone in our growth.
The award also endorses our position at the centre of a number of critical programmes across government. Importantly, it also provides greater visibility over future revenues and underpins the Board's confidence in upgrading its expectations for FY27 while reinforcing our confidence in the Group's medium-term growth trajectory. We look forward to working alongside our consortium partners over the coming years."
*
Current market expectations prior to this announcement for FY27 were revenue of £60.3 million and adjusted EBITDA of £6.0 million.

FY26 FULL YEAR TRADING UPDATE
69% growth in Adjusted EBITDA1 to £5.9m
FY26 expected to be ahead of recently upgraded market expectations
London, 30 June 2026
-
Made Tech Group Plc
, (AIM:MTEC) a leading provider of digital, data and technology services to the UK public sector, is pleased to announce a trading update for the year ended 31 May 2026 ("FY26").
FY26 highlights (unaudited)
·
Revenue of £58.9m ahead of market expectations

Adjusted EBITDA

·

Continued commercial momentum
·

including the recently awarded £19m contract with the Government Digital Service and a healthy Contracted Backlog

·
Made Tech remains well positioned to benefit from the UK Governments' Spending Review announced in June 2025 and available from April 2026
·
AI is creating new product & growth opportunities
·
Made Tech will release its FY26 results in September and will provide an update on current trading at that time
Rory MacDonald, Chief Executive Officer, commented:
"FY26 has been a transformational year for Made Tech. We have delivered strong revenue growth, materially improved profitability and cash generation, and have entered FY27 with significant positive momentum in our business. The UK public sector is entering a multi-decade AI transformation, creating a substantial long-term opportunity for trusted delivery partners like Made Tech. Recent contract awards reinforce our position at the centre of a number of critical programmes across government. With a strong balance sheet, high earnings visibility and an increasingly differentiated proposition, we believe Made Tech is well positioned to capitalise on these opportunities and we look forward to FY27 with confidence."
Notes:
All financials are based on unaudited figures.

3
Sales Bookings represent the total value of sales contracts awarded in the Period, to be delivered in FY26-FY30. Net Sales Bookings includes the value of sales contracts previously recognised that lapsed during the Period.

company_30s.what_they_do: Made Tech Group PLC is a UK‑based software and services provider that builds and delivers digital platforms for public‑sector organisations, especially the government and local authorities.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Its products enable agencies to modernise citizen services, manage data securely and comply with regulatory frameworks. The market for digital government solutions is growing rapidly, and Made Tech has positioned itself as a specialist in that niche, giving it a defensible moat against generic cloud vendors.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a growth phase, having recently secured several large contracts that will drive revenue for the next few years. It has a stable cash position, a new CFO, and a leadership team that is actively steering the firm toward profitability.

rns_narrative: Made Tech has been signing progressively larger government contracts – the latest on 18 Aug 2026 is the biggest ever for the firm, followed by a £19 m deal in April. These wins signal a clear demand for its services.
Management updates show a focus on financial discipline: a new CFO, leadership changes, and a positive FY26 trading update. The company is tightening governance while keeping an eye on cash flow.
The narrative now revolves around a sustained contract pipeline that should lift earnings, with the company moving from a period of uncertainty to one of steady revenue growth.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: The community is quietly optimistic about a lift‑off, driven by a handful of traders who see volume spikes as a prelude to a big move.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Traders on Primetip are calling the recent volume surge a sign that market makers are ready to push the stock up, citing the new contracts and the fact that the stock is trading deep below its historical peaks.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: A small group of skeptics worry that the firm may still be over‑dependent on a single large contract and that liquidity could be thin if the price continues to slide.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Initially neutral, the chatter turned bullish within the first hour after the latest contract announcement, but the overall volume remains modest, suggesting the crowd is still cautious.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat, indicating no public search interest – a classic contrarian signal that a surprise could be on the horizon.

near_term_catalysts: The formal signing of the 18 Aug contract and any accompanying revenue‑recognition announcement.
A Q3 earnings report that beats analyst expectations, especially if it shows the new contract’s impact on the income statement.
A sudden uptick in trading volume that exceeds the 3‑month average, signalling institutional buying.
Price testing the key support zone that has held since the last bottom – a bounce from this level would be a textbook mean‑reversion trigger.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals include a sustained volume spike (≥2× the daily average), a breakout above the recent high of the 52‑week range, and the appearance of a bullish chart pattern such as a double bottom or a bullish engulfing candle. Any negative earnings guidance or a cancellation of a major contract would be a red flag.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the late stage of a crash‑recovery cycle. The APEX score indicates tight compression, so a breakout is likely soon if the catalyst arrives. The market has already taken the bulk of the downside, so the next move will be a mean‑reversion to about half the peak.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The firm sits at a deep crash level (70‑95 % down) and has just secured a record contract that will lift earnings for several quarters. Historically, RED signals in this depth have delivered >160 % returns. If the price climbs to roughly 50 % of its all‑time high, that represents a 2‑3× gain from the current level, while the downside risk is capped at the remaining 70‑90 % of the peak.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the new contract is delayed or the company fails to meet the revenue targets, the stock could slide further to 10 % of its peak. The primary risk is a loss of institutional interest and thin liquidity that could leave the price stuck at a new low.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Upside potential: 2‑3× (200‑300 % return). Downside risk: 70‑90 % of the peak. The asymmetry is favourable for a contrarian play – a modest loss in the first few weeks could be outweighed by a substantial rebound.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a confirmed volume spike and a retest of the support zone. Allocate 10‑15 % of your discretionary equity to the position, set a stop 20 % below the entry to protect against a prolonged slide, and use a trailing stop to lock in gains once the price moves above the 50 % recovery level.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a sustained volume increase (≥2× the 30‑day average) and a clear breakout above the recent high. Use a price‑based trigger: once the stock clears the key resistance area, consider a small partial entry while keeping the rest of the allocation on standby.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no immediate delisting or bankruptcy risks. The main concern is a failure to deliver on the new contract or a significant earnings miss.

ai_insights.bottom_line: A deep crash coupled with a fresh, large government contract creates a 2‑3× upside if mean reversion hits the halfway mark, while the risk of a further slide is limited to the remaining 70‑90 % of the peak.
